from.name: Livingston PortMaster Network Access Server ecosystem

to.name: RADIUS
to.historical_term: Remote Authentication Dial In User Service

property: A centralized NAS authentication/service-configuration protocol is developed by Livingston to solve the account/policy administration problem of its PortMaster network access server family, then enters the IETF standards process.

date_or_range.notes: RFC 2058 documents the original Livingston/PortMaster development but does not by itself give the first internal release date.

sources.locator: RFC 2058 Acknowledgments: RADIUS originally developed by Livingston Enterprises for PortMaster series; Introduction for modem-pool/NAS problem
sources.supports: direct product-to-protocol origin and operational motivation

sources.locator: PortMaster Configuration Guide, PPP/SLIP/PAP/CHAP access operation
sources.supports: contemporary PortMaster NAS environment that requires centralized subscriber authentication/service policy
sources.notes: Product manual supplies deployment context; RFC 2058 supplies the explicit ancestry statement.

negative_claims: This edge does not claim that all later RADIUS use cases were requirements of the original PortMaster design.
This edge does not claim that 802.1X, Wi-Fi, VPN, broadband or network-device administration were original RADIUS target environments.
This edge does not claim that every later AAA protocol derives from RADIUS.
This edge does not yet establish the date or source revision of the first pre-RFC Livingston RADIUS implementation.
open_questions: Locate the earliest Livingston RADIUS daemon/client source release and establish its date/provenance.
Identify the first PortMaster/ComOS release with RADIUS client support.
Recover early RADIUS users/clients/dictionary formats and vendor-specific attributes.
Trace RADIUS adoption beyond dial-up NAS only with explicit deployment/standards evidence.
Build separate lineages for RADIUS Accounting, 802.1X/EAP use, Diameter, and RadSec.
notes: High-confidence product-to-protocol genealogy because the RFC itself names Livingston and PortMaster as the original development context.
